exploration.title: Shape Slicer
exploration.subject: Mathematics
exploration.summary: Predict, make and measure plane sections of a cube, tetrahedron or sphere while controlling orientation and plane height.
exploration.question: How can one plane make different two-dimensional sections from the same solid?
exploration.explanation: A cross-section is the two-dimensional intersection of a solid and a plane, not a shadow, outer face or thick physical slice. Rotating a solid relative to a fixed plane can change which faces and edges the plane meets. Moving a parallel plane through a sphere changes circle size but not the circular shape until tangency. Camera motion changes only the view. This ideal model reports computed area and boundary length in model units; readouts are rounded and omit material thickness, deformation and measurement uncertainty.

experiments.title: Rotate a cube
experiments.instruction: Predict whether every central cube section must have four sides. Keep the side-2 cube and plane height 0 fixed; change only cube orientation from face-parallel to the diagonal preset.
experiments.observe: The face-parallel section is a 4-sided square with area 4.00. The diagonal plane reaches six faces and makes a 6-sided hexagon with area 5.20. Explain the result from the intersected faces, not the cube silhouette.

experiments.title: Move through a sphere
experiments.instruction: Predict whether shape, size or both change. Keep the radius-1 sphere and plane orientation fixed; change only plane height from 0 to 0.6 and compare the equal-scale straight-on sections.
experiments.observe: Both sections are circles. Radius decreases from 1.00 to 0.80 and area from 3.14 to 2.01 square units, 64% of the central area. Explain why parallel sections shrink toward tangency.

exploration.misconception: Square cube faces do not force every cube section to be square. A plane that misses the solid makes no section; a tangent plane can meet at a point or line with zero area.
